extracted.intended_audience: journalists, reporters, photographers, editors and news organizations submitting work for the George Polk Awards (including the Sydney H. Schanberg Prize)
extracted.subtask_description: Submission and selection criteria for the George Polk Awards in Journalism (including the Sydney H. Schanberg Prize), describing eligible media, the qualities judges prize (investigative, intrepid, resourceful reporting), and specific requirements for the Schanberg long-form prize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on intrepid, bold, and influential reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The awards 'focus[] on the intrepid, bold, and influential work of the reporters themselves.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis is on the reporter's courage and influence — recognition is directed at individual reporters' work rather than institutional promotion. Examples on the page highlight war reporting, deep investigations, and impactful storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premium on investigative work that is original, resourceful, and thought-provoking
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges 'place a premium on investigative work that is original, resourceful, and thought-provoking.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigative entries should demonstrate originality of approach, resourcefulness (requiring digging), and the capacity to provoke thought; the site reiterates that winning work 'requires digging and resourcefulness, and brings results.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility across media types
rubrics_metrics.description: Winners are chosen from 'newspapers, magazines, television, radio and online news organizations.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All traditional and digital news media are eligible — the award recognizes reporting 'across all media.' Submissions may come from any of these formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact / reporting that 'brings results'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should demonstrate tangible impact (policy change, accountability, public awareness, further investigation, etc.). The site explicitly cites results as a factor judges consider when conferring awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sydney H. Schanberg Prize — long-form investigative/enterprise journalism requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Schanberg Prize is 'Awarded annually by George Polk judges for exceptional long-form investigative or enterprise journalism. Articles must be at least 5,000 words in length and represent highly distinguished, deep coverage' of certain serious topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required: minimum length 5,000 words; subject-matter scope includes armed conflicts; local, state or Federal government corruption; military injustice; war crimes, genocide or sedition; or authoritarian government abuses. The prize honors deep, distinguished coverage of those topics and is awarded annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Powerful Photography
rubrics_metrics.description: One award category emphasizes 'Powerful Photography' (e.g., images of conflict or human consequence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographic entries are recognized for their power to convey story and impact; page examples include conflict and human-suffering imagery. Photography from newspapers or other outlets is eligible under the general media eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: In-depth Articles
rubrics_metrics.description: One category highlights 'In-depth Articles' (extended reporting on complex events or issues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In-depth pieces should provide comprehensive examinations of topics (example cited: investigation of the causes, course and aftermath of the January 6 attack). The Schanberg Prize is a specialized long-form instance of this broader category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Exposés
rubrics_metrics.description: One category is labeled 'Exposés' (reporting that uncovers dangers, wrongdoing or hidden facts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exposé entries should reveal significant, previously unreported problems or dangers (example: reporting on faulty sleep apnea machines). Emphasis on investigative methods that surface important public-interest facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Another category is 'Investigations' (systematic examination of sources, causes, and effects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigative pieces are expected to examine sources and effects of issues (example: examination of sources and effects of deadly particulate pollutants). Depth, evidence-gathering and analysis are implied criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Significant Enterprise
rubrics_metrics.description: A category called 'Significant Enterprise' recognizes substantial enterprise reporting and narrative work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This category rewards ambitious, sustained enterprise reporting (example: narrative dispatches about daily life in Ukrainian trenches). Entries should demonstrate significant reporter initiative and substantial reporting effort.
